text: At 65', Seabrook Town increased pressing intensity (PPDA from 0.66 to 0.84), raised their defensive line height (0.60 to 0.72), and chose more direct attacking routes (directness from 0.42 to 0.57) to trigger higher pressing and faster transitions in an attempt to overturn a 2-1 deficit[#1361]. However, this shift led to a decline in their expected goals (xG from 0.61 to 0.43) and a significant drop in field tilt (70.7% to 45.7%), indicating Harbour City’s effective rest-defense and compact patient short-passing system blunted Seabrook’s forward momentum[#1361]. Seabrook’s wide 3-4-3 formation and crossing-based style failed to achieve overloads or penetrate effectively, shown by fewer box touches and reduced shot volumes post-change[#1361]. Harbour City’s lower PPDA (5.4 in last 10 minutes) and disciplined midfield minimized turnovers and controlled progression, highlighting their tactical resilience under pressure[#1361].
